title: Claude Hot Path: One-File API Clients in 7 Languages
summary: Open-source toolkit offers minimal Claude API clients in Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C#, Java, and Ruby without SDK dependencies.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Claude Hot Path provides single-file API clients in seven programming languages, eliminating the need for official SDK installations or external dependencies.
- Each implementation handles authentication, streaming responses, and error handling in under 300 lines of idiomatic code for immediate integration.
- The MIT-licensed toolkit targets developers who need fast prototyping or minimal dependency footprints in production environments across diverse language stacks.


Developers working with Anthropic's Claude API now have a lightweight alternative to official SDKs. Claude Hot Path, officially launched on November 23, 2026, delivers single-file API clients in Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C#, Java, and Ruby. Each implementation requires zero external dependencies beyond standard HTTP libraries, allowing teams to integrate Claude's capabilities without package manager overhead or version conflicts.


## Architecture and Implementation Details


The toolkit structures each client as a self-contained module under 300 lines of code. Every implementation handles OAuth bearer token authentication, streaming chat completions, function calling, and exponential backoff retry logic. The Python client uses only the standard library's urllib and json modules, while the JavaScript version relies solely on Node.js fetch. Go leverages net/http, Rust uses reqwest as its single external crate, and the remaining languages follow similar minimal-dependency patterns.


Creator AndyCross designed the repository for scenarios where full SDK installations create friction. Each file includes inline documentation covering initialization, message formatting, and error handling. The streaming implementation processes server-sent events incrementally, enabling real-time response rendering without buffering entire completions in memory.


## Language-Specific Optimizations


The repository's language implementations reflect idiomatic patterns for their respective ecosystems. The Rust client exposes async/await interfaces with Result types for compile-time error safety. The C# version integrates IAsyncEnumerable for LINQ-compatible streaming, while Java provides CompletableFuture wrappers for reactive pipeline compatibility. The Go implementation uses channels for concurrent request handling, and the Ruby client leverages blocks for iterator-style response processing.


- Python and JavaScript clients support both synchronous and async execution modes
- Rust and Go versions prioritize zero-allocation streaming for high-throughput scenarios
- All implementations include configurable timeout and retry parameters


## Practical Use Cases


The toolkit addresses three primary developer workflows. First, rapid prototyping sessions where installing full SDKs slows iteration cycles. Second, embedded systems or edge environments with constrained dependency budgets. Third, polyglot teams standardizing Claude integration patterns across microservices written in different languages. The MIT license permits unrestricted modification, allowing teams to fork and extend functionality for proprietary use cases.


## Availability and Community Response


The project launched today on GitHub with full source code, examples, and contribution guidelines. Early community feedback on Hacker News highlights the utility for serverless functions and container deployments where layer size directly impacts cold start latency. The repository includes test suites demonstrating integration with Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 and[Claude Sonnet](https://emergent.sh/integrations/claude-sonnet) 4.5 models, though the clients remain model-agnostic and compatible with any Claude API endpoint.


## What This Means


Claude Hot Path represents a pragmatic shift toward developer-first AI integration tooling. By eliminating SDK lock-in and dependency sprawl, the project lowers barriers for teams adopting Claude across heterogeneous technology stacks. The single-file approach also simplifies auditing and customization, particularly for organizations with strict security review processes. As AI capabilities become infrastructure primitives, minimal-footprint clients like these enable more flexible architectural choices without sacrificing access to frontier model capabilities.
